propositions: Ticket directory creation via os.makedirs outside the write lock leaves a window where an interruption (kill, timeout, host sleep) strands an empty directory, reported by fsck as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

New staging.py module stages directory and first event file together in a dot-prefixed temporary path (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>), then publishes them atomically via os.rename under the existing write lock.

Temp-path naming convention makes staging directories invisible to fsck scanners (_ticket_dirs, foreign_store_path_list, JSON check, relation_snapshot) through existing dot-prefix exclusion rules, requiring zero scanner changes.

Both single-event (stage_and_commit) and batch (batch_stage_and_commit) paths are converted to use StagedEvent.promote(), plus inbound_translate._write_event_file and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission.

Bounded best-effort sweep_stale_staging() reclaims only .tmp-newticket-* directories owned by provably dead processes (using v2 host+pid-namespace+start-time stamp), respecting 043f boundary by never touching ticket directories or store data.

Byte parity and event format remain unchanged; canonical_bytes/canonical_str serialization unchanged; all 466 store tests, 3067 reconciler/bridge/concurrency tests, and 9 new atomic-create tests pass.
